---- MODULE W4Od3m4p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets, Sequences

Slots == {"L1", "L2"}
Jobs == {"j1", "j2", "j3"}
NONE == "none"
MaxQ == 2

VARIABLES queue, owner, reserv, active, admin

vars == <<queue, owner, reserv, active, admin>>

NoRes == [job |-> NONE, slot |-> NONE]

Init ==
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ reserv = NoRes
    /\ active = {}
    /\ admin = FALSE

Submit(j) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < MaxQ
    /\ j \notin active
    /\ \A i \in DOMAIN queue : queue[i] # j
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, j)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, reserv, active, admin>>

Reserve(s) ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ reserv = NoRes
    /\ owner[s] = NONE
    /\ reserv' = [job |-> Head(queue), slot |-> s]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, active, admin>>

Commit ==
    /\ reserv # NoRes
    /\ owner[reserv.slot] = NONE
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![reserv.slot] = reserv.job]
    /\ active' = active \cup {reserv.job}
    /\ reserv' = NoRes
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, admin>>

Complete(s) ==
    /\ owner[s] # NONE
    /\ active' = active \ {owner[s]}
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, reserv, admin>>

AdminOverride(s) ==
    /\ ~admin
    /\ admin' = TRUE
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ active' = IF owner[s] = NONE THEN active ELSE active \ {owner[s]}
    /\ reserv' = IF reserv.slot = s THEN NoRes ELSE reserv
    /\ UNCHANGED queue

Next ==
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Submit(j)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Reserve(s)
    \/ Commit
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Complete(s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : AdminOverride(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in [Slots -> Jobs \cup {NONE}]
    /\ reserv \in [job : Jobs \cup {NONE}, slot : Slots \cup {NONE}]
    /\ active \subseteq Jobs
    /\ admin \in BOOLEAN
    /\ \A i \in DOMAIN queue : queue[i] \in Jobs

NoDoubleAlloc ==
    (reserv # NoRes) => (owner[reserv.slot] = NONE)

====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAlloc
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement engine processes settlement jobs against a fixed
set of settlement slots (one slot per correspondent-account ledger line). Jobs
arrive into a bounded admission queue: because downstream capacity is limited,
the queue applies backpressure and refuses to admit a new job once it is full.
Allocation is two-phase so that a slot is never handed to two jobs at once.
First, an admitted job at the head of the queue is *reserved* against a
currently-free slot (the reservation records which job and which slot). Then the
reservation is *committed*, which makes the job the owner of that slot. When a
settlement finishes, the slot is released back to the free pool. A privileged
admin override may forcibly release a slot and clear any in-flight reservation
that targets it (for example to unstick a stalled correspondent), but it only
ever frees slots, it never assigns ownership directly. The engine only reserves
a slot that is currently free.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A job is never reserved against a slot that already has an owner, so the same slot is never allocated to two jobs at once.

---- MODULE W4Od16m6p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Pharms == {"p1", "p2"}
NONE == "none"
LEASE == 2
MaxClock == 4
MaxVer == 4

VARIABLES version, owner, exp, clock, staged, admin

vars == <<version, owner, exp, clock, staged, admin>>

NoStage == [who |-> NONE, base |-> -1]

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ owner = NONE
    /\ exp = 0
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ staged = NoStage
    /\ admin = FALSE

Acquire(p) ==
    /\ (owner = NONE) \/ (clock >= exp)
    /\ owner' = p
    /\ exp' = clock + LEASE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, clock, staged, admin>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ owner' = IF owner # NONE /\ clock + 1 >= exp THEN NONE ELSE owner
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, exp, staged, admin>>

Prepare(p) ==
    /\ owner = p
    /\ clock < exp
    /\ staged = NoStage
    /\ staged' = [who |-> p, base |-> version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, owner, exp, clock, admin>>

Apply ==
    /\ staged # NoStage
    /\ owner = staged.who
    /\ clock < exp
    /\ staged.base = version
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ staged' = NoStage
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, exp, clock, admin>>

Release ==
    /\ owner # NONE
    /\ owner' = NONE
    /\ staged' = NoStage
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, exp, clock, admin>>

AdminOverride ==
    /\ ~admin
    /\ admin' = TRUE
    /\ owner' = NONE
    /\ staged' = NoStage
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, exp, clock>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Pharms : Acquire(p)
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E p \in Pharms : Prepare(p)
    \/ Apply
    \/ Release
    \/ AdminOverride

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ owner \in Pharms \cup {NONE}
    /\ exp \in 0..(MaxClock + LEASE)
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxClock
    /\ staged \in [who : Pharms \cup {NONE}, base : -1..MaxVer]
    /\ admin \in BOOLEAN

NoLostUpdate ==
    (staged # NoStage) => (staged.base = version)

====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A pharmacy dispensing system keeps one shared prescription record per patient
that pharmacists edit concurrently. To prevent lost updates, editing is guarded
by a time-limited lease: a pharmacist must acquire the exclusive lease before
touching the record, and the lease automatically expires after a fixed number of
clock ticks. Editing is read-modify-write: while holding a valid lease a
pharmacist first *prepares* an update, recording the record version it observed;
the prepared update is then *applied*, which bumps the record version, but only
if the lease is still valid and no other version change has slipped in since the
value was read. A background clock tick advances time and revokes any lease that
has reached its expiry, and a pharmacist may also voluntarily release the lease
early, discarding any prepared-but-unapplied update. A privileged admin override may forcibly revoke the lease
and discard any prepared-but-unapplied update (for instance to clear a jammed
terminal); the admin override never itself edits the record or changes its
version.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever an update is prepared and waiting, the version it was based on still equals the record's current version, so no committed edit can silently overwrite another.

---- MODULE W4Od15m5p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Members == {"m1", "m2", "m3"}
Orders == {"o1", "o2", "o3"}
NONE == "none"
CAP == 2
QUORUM == 2

VARIABLES book, pending, votes, crashed

vars == <<book, pending, votes, crashed>>

Init ==
    /\ book = {}
    /\ pending = NONE
    /\ votes = [m \in Members |-> FALSE]
    /\ crashed = {}

Propose(o) ==
    /\ pending = NONE
    /\ o \notin book
    /\ pending' = o
    /\ votes' = [m \in Members |-> FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, crashed>>

Vote(m) ==
    /\ pending # NONE
    /\ m \notin crashed
    /\ ~votes[m]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![m] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, pending, crashed>>

Crash(m) ==
    /\ m \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, pending, votes>>

Commit ==
    /\ pending # NONE
    /\ Cardinality({m \in Members : votes[m]}) >= QUORUM
    /\ Cardinality(book) < CAP
    /\ book' = book \cup {pending}
    /\ pending' = NONE
    /\ votes' = [m \in Members |-> FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED crashed

Withdraw ==
    /\ pending # NONE
    /\ pending' = NONE
    /\ votes' = [m \in Members |-> FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, crashed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E o \in Orders : Propose(o)
    \/ \E m \in Members : Vote(m)
    \/ \E m \in Members : Crash(m)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Withdraw

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ book \subseteq Orders
    /\ pending \in Orders \cup {NONE}
    /\ votes \in [Members -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Members

WithinCapacity ==
    Cardinality(book) <= CAP

====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT WithinCapacity
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction whose matched book can hold at most a
fixed number of cleared orders (its capacity). Admitting a new order into the
book is a committee decision: a member proposes a candidate order, and each
auction member votes yes on the standing proposal. A proposal is committed into
the book only once a quorum of yes votes has been gathered, and even then only if
the book still has spare capacity. Any member may crash silently at any time;
a crashed member simply stops voting and never recovers, so if too many crash a
proposal can no longer reach quorum. To keep the auction live, a standing
proposal may be withdrawn (cleared without admission) at any time, for instance
when it cannot gather enough votes.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of orders committed into the matched book never exceeds the auction's fixed capacity.

Controllers == {"c1", "c2", "c3"}
NONE == "none"

vars == <<reg, inCS, reqs, grants>>

Init ==
    /\ reg = NONE
    /\ inCS = {}
    /\ reqs = {}
    /\ grants = {}

Request(c) ==
    /\ c \notin inCS
    /\ reg # c
    /\ c \notin reqs
    /\ c \notin grants
    /\ reqs' = reqs \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, inCS, grants>>

Grant(c) ==
    /\ c \in reqs
    /\ reg = NONE
    /\ reg' = c
    /\ reqs' = reqs \ {c}
    /\ grants' = grants \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED inCS

Fail(c) ==
    /\ c \in reqs
    /\ reg # NONE
    /\ reqs' = reqs \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, inCS, grants>>

Enter(c) ==
    /\ c \in grants
    /\ reg = c
    /\ inCS' = inCS \cup {c}
    /\ grants' = grants \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, reqs>>

Exit(c) ==
    /\ c \in inCS
    /\ inCS' = inCS \ {c}
    /\ reg' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reqs, grants>>

    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Request(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Grant(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Fail(c)

    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Exit(c)

    /\ inCS \subseteq Controllers

    \A c \in Controllers : (c \in inCS) => (reg = c)

====

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutexCoherent
nl:
A power-grid load-shedding controller cluster protects one critical actuator
(the feeder breaker) that only a single controller may drive at a time. Mutual
exclusion is arbitrated by a compare-and-swap lock register that holds the
identity of the current holder, or nothing when free. Controllers coordinate
over an asynchronous fabric where messages may be delivered in any order. A
controller that wants the actuator emits an acquire request; requests sit in a
pool and are serviced in arbitrary order. Servicing a request is a
compare-and-swap: if the register is free it is atomically set to the requester
and a grant notification is emitted, otherwise the request simply fails and is
dropped (the controller may request again). On receiving its grant a controller
enters the critical section and starts driving the actuator; when finished it
exits, which frees the register. Grant notifications also travel through the pool
and may be reordered relative to other messages.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Any controller currently in the critical section is exactly the controller named in the lock register, so at most one controller ever drives the actuator.

---- MODULE W4Od2m4p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets, Sequences

Tasks == {"t1", "t2"}
Robots == {"r1", "r2"}
MaxQ == 2
MaxGen == 2

VARIABLES queue, curGen, grant, dispatched, done

vars == <<queue, curGen, grant, dispatched, done>>

Seen(t) ==
    \/ \E i \in DOMAIN queue : queue[i] = t
    \/ \E m \in dispatched : m.task = t

Init ==
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ curGen = 0
    /\ grant = [r \in Robots |-> -1]
    /\ dispatched = {}
    /\ done = {}

Enqueue(t) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < MaxQ
    /\ ~Seen(t)
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, t)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<curGen, grant, dispatched, done>>

Authorize(r) ==
    /\ grant[r] # curGen
    /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![r] = curGen]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, curGen, dispatched, done>>

Deauthorize(r) ==
    /\ grant[r] # -1
    /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![r] = -1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, curGen, dispatched, done>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ curGen < MaxGen
    /\ curGen' = curGen + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, grant, dispatched, done>>

Dispatch(r) ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ grant[r] = curGen
    /\ dispatched' = dispatched \cup {[task |-> Head(queue), robot |-> r, gen |-> curGen]}
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<curGen, grant, done>>

Execute(m) ==
    /\ m \in dispatched
    /\ m \notin done
    /\ grant[m.robot] = curGen
    /\ m.gen = curGen
    /\ done' = done \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, curGen, grant, dispatched>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Tasks : Enqueue(t)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Authorize(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Deauthorize(r)
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Dispatch(r)
    \/ \E m \in dispatched : Execute(m)

TypeOK ==
    /\ curGen \in 0..MaxGen
    /\ grant \in [Robots -> (-1)..MaxGen]
    /\ dispatched \subseteq [task : Tasks, robot : Robots, gen : 0..MaxGen]
    /\ done \subseteq [task : Tasks, robot : Robots, gen : 0..MaxGen]
    /\ \A i \in DOMAIN queue : queue[i] \in Tasks

AuthorizedExecution ==
    done \subseteq dispatched

====

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AuthorizedExecution
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet pulls pick tasks from a central dispatcher. Tasks enter a
bounded dispatch queue that applies backpressure and refuses new tasks when full.
Robots must be authorized before they may work: an authorization stamps a robot
with the fleet's current configuration generation. A reconfiguration bumps the
generation (for instance after a safety re-survey), which makes previously
granted authorizations stale until the robot is re-authorized. To hand out work,
the dispatcher takes the head task and, only for a robot whose authorization
matches the current generation, emits an assignment message tagged with that
task, robot, and generation. Assignment messages travel over an asynchronous bus
and may be delivered in any order. A robot may also be stood down (deauthorized) at any time, dropping its
authorization. A robot executes an assignment only when it
still holds a current-generation authorization, and the completed work is
recorded. Every recorded execution must correspond to a genuine assignment the
dispatcher actually issued to that robot.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every recorded task execution corresponds to an assignment that was actually dispatched to that robot, so no unauthorized or stale robot's action is ever recorded.

---- MODULE W4Od11m3p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Nodes == {"n1", "n2"}
NONE == "none"
MaxTerm == 3
MaxVer == 3

VARIABLES term, leader, leaderOf, version, pool, acked

vars == <<term, leader, leaderOf, version, pool, acked>>

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ leaderOf = [t \in 1..MaxTerm |-> NONE]
    /\ version = 0
    /\ pool = {}
    /\ acked = {}

Elect(n) ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leaderOf' = [leaderOf EXCEPT ![term + 1] = n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, pool, acked>>

Fail ==
    /\ leader # NONE
    /\ leader' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leaderOf, version, pool, acked>>

Recover ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ term >= 1
    /\ leaderOf[term] # NONE
    /\ leader' = leaderOf[term]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leaderOf, version, pool, acked>>

Submit(n) ==
    /\ leader = n
    /\ pool' = pool \cup {[by |-> n, term |-> term, base |-> version]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, leaderOf, version, acked>>

Apply(w) ==
    /\ w \in pool
    /\ w.by = leader
    /\ w.term = term
    /\ w.base = version
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ pool' = pool \ {w}
    /\ acked' = acked \cup {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, leaderOf>>

Drop(w) ==
    /\ w \in pool
    /\ (w.term # term \/ w.by # leader)
    /\ pool' = pool \ {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, leaderOf, version, acked>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
    \/ Fail
    \/ Recover
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Submit(n)
    \/ \E w \in pool : Apply(w)
    \/ \E w \in pool : Drop(w)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {NONE}
    /\ leaderOf \in [1..MaxTerm -> Nodes \cup {NONE}]
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ pool \subseteq [by : Nodes, term : 1..MaxTerm, base : 0..MaxVer]
    /\ acked \subseteq [by : Nodes, term : 1..MaxTerm, base : 0..MaxVer]

WriteAuthorship ==
    \A w \in pool : w.by = leaderOf[w.term]

====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT WriteAuthorship
nl:
A print-shop job spooler cluster keeps one shared spool-configuration record.
Only the elected leader may write to it. Leadership runs in strictly increasing
terms: each election starts a fresh term and installs exactly one leader for that
term, and the cluster remembers which node led each term. The leader can fail
(failover); after a failure the same term's recorded leader may recover and
resume, or a brand-new election can advance to the next term with a new leader.
Writes are asynchronous and reorderable: the leader submits a write carrying its
identity, its term, and the record version it read; submitted writes sit in a
pool and are processed in any order. A write is applied (bumping the record
version) only if it comes from the current leader in the current term and its
base version still matches, which prevents one update from silently clobbering
another. Writes that are stale or not from the current leader are dropped from
the pool.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every write sitting in the pool was authored by the very node that was elected leader for that write's term, so no competing or stale leader can inject a lost update.

---- MODULE W4Od9m0p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Operators == {"o1", "o2", "o3"}
MaxVer == 3

VARIABLES version, authorized, attempts, approved, admin

vars == <<version, authorized, attempts, approved, admin>>

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ authorized = {}
    /\ attempts = {}
    /\ approved = {}
    /\ admin = FALSE

Authorize(op) ==
    /\ op \notin authorized
    /\ authorized' = authorized \cup {op}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, attempts, approved, admin>>

Revoke(op) ==
    /\ op \in authorized
    /\ authorized' = authorized \ {op}
    /\ attempts' = {a \in attempts : a.op # op}
    /\ approved' = {a \in approved : a.op # op}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, admin>>

Begin(op) ==
    /\ \A a \in attempts : a.op # op
    /\ \A a \in approved : a.op # op
    /\ attempts' = attempts \cup {[op |-> op, base |-> version]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, authorized, approved, admin>>

Retry(a) ==
    /\ a \in attempts
    /\ a.base # version
    /\ attempts' = (attempts \ {a}) \cup {[op |-> a.op, base |-> version]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, authorized, approved, admin>>

Approve(a) ==
    /\ a \in attempts
    /\ a.op \in authorized
    /\ a.base = version
    /\ approved = {}
    /\ attempts' = attempts \ {a}
    /\ approved' = {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, authorized, admin>>

Apply(a) ==
    /\ a \in approved
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ approved' = approved \ {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, attempts, admin>>

AdminOverride ==
    /\ ~admin
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ admin' = TRUE
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ approved' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, attempts>>

Next ==
    \/ \E op \in Operators : Authorize(op)
    \/ \E op \in Operators : Revoke(op)
    \/ \E op \in Operators : Begin(op)
    \/ \E a \in attempts : Retry(a)
    \/ \E a \in attempts : Approve(a)
    \/ \E a \in approved : Apply(a)
    \/ AdminOverride

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ authorized \subseteq Operators
    /\ attempts \subseteq [op : Operators, base : 0..MaxVer]
    /\ approved \subseteq [op : Operators, base : 0..MaxVer]
    /\ admin \in BOOLEAN

NoStaleUnauthorized ==
    \A a \in approved : (a.op \in authorized) /\ (a.base = version)

====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleUnauthorized
nl:
A power-grid load-shedding controller applies shedding commands to a shared grid
configuration using optimistic concurrency. Operators must be authorized to act,
and the authorized set changes over time as operators are granted or revoked.
An operator begins a command by optimistically reading the current configuration
version. If the version has since moved on, the operator retries by re-reading.
To commit, an authorized operator whose read version still matches the current
version gets its command approved; at most one command may be approved at a time.
An approved command is then applied, which advances the configuration version.
If an operator is revoked while it still holds an approved command, that command
is discarded. Finally, a privileged admin override may force a configuration
change directly, discarding any pending approved command and advancing the
version on its own authority.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Any command currently approved for application belongs to a still-authorized operator and is still based on the current version, so no unauthorized or stale command is ever applied.

NONE == "none"

    /\ votes = {}
    /\ leaderOf = [e \in 1..MaxEpoch |-> NONE]

    /\ candidate' = NONE
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, leader, leaderOf, log>>

Win ==
    /\ candidate # NONE
    /\ Cardinality(votes) >= QUORUM
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ leader' = candidate
    /\ leaderOf' = [leaderOf EXCEPT ![epoch + 1] = candidate]
    /\ candidate' = NONE
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED log

Fail ==
    /\ leader # NONE
    /\ leader' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, candidate, votes, leaderOf, log>>

Dispense(n) ==
    /\ leader = n
    /\ log' = log \cup {[by |-> n, epoch |-> epoch]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, leader, candidate, votes, leaderOf>>

AdminDispense ==
    /\ log' = log \cup {[by |-> ADMIN, epoch |-> epoch]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, leader, candidate, votes, leaderOf>>

Next ==

    \/ \E n \in Terminals : CastVote(n)
    \/ Abort
    \/ Win
    \/ Fail
    \/ \E n \in Terminals : Dispense(n)
    \/ AdminDispense

    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ leader \in Terminals \cup {NONE}
    /\ candidate \in Terminals \cup {NONE}
    /\ votes \subseteq Terminals
    /\ leaderOf \in [1..MaxEpoch -> Terminals \cup {NONE}]
    /\ log \subseteq [by : Terminals \cup {ADMIN}, epoch : 0..MaxEpoch]

DispenseAuthority ==
    \A e \in log : (e.by = ADMIN) \/ (e.epoch \in 1..MaxEpoch /\ e.by = leaderOf[e.epoch])

====

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DispenseAuthority
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser is served by a cluster of dispensing terminals,
but only one may be the active lead terminal at a time. Leadership is decided by
election: any terminal may nominate itself as candidate, the other terminals cast
votes, and once a quorum of votes is gathered the candidate wins and becomes the
lead terminal for a new, higher epoch (the cluster remembers which terminal led
each epoch). An election in progress may also be abandoned, clearing the
candidate and votes. The lead terminal can fail (failover), after which a new

A subway signalling block system admits trains into a track section whose
occupancy must never exceed its capacity. The capacity itself changes at runtime
as maintenance opens or closes running lines: it may be raised freely, or lowered,
but never lowered below the current occupancy (you cannot evict a train already in
the section). Admission uses optimistic concurrency. A waiting train first
requests entry, joining the waiting pool. It then begins an optimistic admission,
reading the current occupancy as its base. If the occupancy has since changed, the
admission is retried by re-reading. A train is actually admitted only if its base
still equals the current occupancy and the occupancy is strictly below capacity;
admission increments the occupancy. A train in the section may later exit,
decrementing the occupancy.

nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch protects one critical resource: exclusive
access to the settlement ledger, which only one node may drive at a time. Granting
this access is done through epoch-numbered reconfiguration. A coordinator proposes
granting the lock to a node, but only while the lock is free and no node is
currently driving the ledger. Each participant must acknowledge the proposal;
participants may be slow but do not fail, so acknowledgements arrive over time and
are never lost. Once every participant has acknowledged, the grant is committed,
which bumps the epoch and installs the proposed node as the current holder. A
proposal may also be abandoned before it commits. Once a node is the holder it may
enter the critical section and drive the ledger, and when it exits, the lock is
released back to free. Because the epoch advances on every committed grant, each
grant is fenced to its own epoch.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Only the node currently recorded as the lock holder is ever in the critical section, so at most one node drives the settlement ledger at a time.

---- MODULE W4Od13m0p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Slots == {"c1", "c2"}
Dispenses == {"d1", "d2"}
NONE == "none"
MaxVer == 2

VARIABLES owner, ver, attempts, pending, admin

vars == <<owner, ver, attempts, pending, admin>>

NoPend == [slot |-> NONE, disp |-> NONE, base |-> -1]

Init ==
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ ver = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ attempts = {}
    /\ pending = NoPend
    /\ admin = FALSE

Begin(s, d) ==
    /\ \A a \in attempts : ~(a.slot = s /\ a.disp = d)
    /\ attempts' = attempts \cup {[slot |-> s, disp |-> d, base |-> ver[s]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, pending, admin>>

Retry(a) ==
    /\ a \in attempts
    /\ a.base # ver[a.slot]
    /\ attempts' = (attempts \ {a}) \cup {[slot |-> a.slot, disp |-> a.disp, base |-> ver[a.slot]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, pending, admin>>

Select(a) ==
    /\ a \in attempts
    /\ pending = NoPend
    /\ a.base = ver[a.slot]
    /\ owner[a.slot] = NONE
    /\ pending' = [slot |-> a.slot, disp |-> a.disp, base |-> a.base]
    /\ attempts' = attempts \ {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, admin>>

Commit ==
    /\ pending # NoPend
    /\ owner[pending.slot] = NONE
    /\ pending.base = ver[pending.slot]
    /\ ver[pending.slot] < MaxVer
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![pending.slot] = pending.disp]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![pending.slot] = ver[pending.slot] + 1]
    /\ pending' = NoPend
    /\ UNCHANGED <<attempts, admin>>

Bump(s) == IF ver[s] < MaxVer THEN ver[s] + 1 ELSE ver[s]

Release(s) ==
    /\ owner[s] # NONE
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![s] = Bump(s)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<attempts, pending, admin>>

CancelPending ==
    /\ pending # NoPend
    /\ pending' = NoPend
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, attempts, admin>>

AdminOverride(s) ==
    /\ ~admin
    /\ owner[s] # NONE
    /\ admin' = TRUE
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![s] = Bump(s)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<attempts, pending>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Slots, d \in Dispenses : Begin(s, d)
    \/ \E a \in attempts : Retry(a)
    \/ \E a \in attempts : Select(a)
    \/ Commit
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Release(s)
    \/ CancelPending
    \/ \E s \in Slots : AdminOverride(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in [Slots -> Dispenses \cup {NONE}]
    /\ ver \in [Slots -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ attempts \subseteq [slot : Slots, disp : Dispenses, base : 0..MaxVer]
    /\ pending \in [slot : Slots \cup {NONE}, disp : Dispenses \cup {NONE}, base : (-1)..MaxVer]
    /\ admin \in BOOLEAN

NoDoubleAlloc ==
    (pending # NoPend) =>
        (owner[pending.slot] = NONE /\ pending.base = ver[pending.slot])

====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAlloc
nl:
A vending-machine network allocates product-column slots to dispense operations,
and no slot may be allocated to two dispenses at once. Allocation uses optimistic
concurrency with a per-slot version number. A dispense operation begins by reading
a slot's current version as its base. If the slot's version has since changed, the
operation retries by re-reading. To allocate, a validated claim is first selected:
a claim may be selected only if its base still equals the slot's current version
and the slot is currently free, and at most one claim is selected at a time.
Selecting a claim does not yet change ownership. The selected claim is then
committed, which makes the dispense the slot's owner and bumps the slot's version.
An owner may release its slot, bumping the version (up to a maximum). A selected
claim may also be cancelled before it commits. Finally, a privileged admin
override may forcibly release an owned slot (for instance to clear a jam), also
bumping the version. A claim is only ever selected against a free slot whose
version still matches.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a claim is selected for commit, its target slot is still free and the version it read still matches, so the same slot is never allocated to two dispenses.
